hub.headline: Rerun vs the tools you already know.
hub.description: How Rerun compares with Zapier, Make, n8n, Lindy, Manus, Claude Cowork and seven more: ease of use, teamwork, flexibility and cost, side by side.
hub.faqTitle: Choosing between Rerun and the rest.

1.question: What is Rerun an alternative to?
1.answer: Rerun replaces workflow tools like Zapier, Make and n8n for tasks that need judgment, credit-metered agent platforms like Lindy, Twin or Dust, and self-hosted agents like OpenClaw or Hermes Agent for teams that do not want to run a server. Each agent lives on your workspace’s private machine and works around the clock.

2.question: Is Rerun an automation tool or an AI agent platform?
2.answer: An AI agent platform. You describe a job in plain words, connect your apps, and the agent plans the steps, remembers what it learned and asks you before anything risky. There is no flowchart to build.

3.question: Can I use Rerun alongside the tools I already have?
3.answer: Yes. Most teams keep their simple automations and developer tools, and hand Rerun the recurring work that keeps breaking or needs someone to think.

4.question: How much does Rerun cost compared with these tools?
4.answer: One plan from {price} a month with a secured private machine, unlimited agents and model credit, and a free 5-day trial. Rerun never bills per task, per credit or per execution, and your agents can run on the ChatGPT or Claude plan you already pay for.

zapier.subtitle: App-to-app automation
zapier.pitch: A Zap moves data between apps. A Rerun agent sorts the inbox, answers the lead and chases the invoice.

easeOfUse.them: You pick the trigger, then every action and field mapping, or let Copilot draft them and maintain them after that.
easeOfUse.rerun: Describe the job in one sentence and connect your apps. No flow to build.

getTheJobDone.them: Runs the same steps: a new email format or a renamed field needs another path.
getTheJobDone.rerun: Handles the cases no one planned, asks when unsure, and reports what’s done.

agentTeamwork.them: Zaps don’t talk to each other: you wire Tables or sub-Zaps between them.
agentTeamwork.rerun: Your agents talk to each other on their own and share one database. Nothing to wire.

collaboration.them: Shared Zaps start on the Team plan, $69 a month for 2,000 tasks.
collaboration.rerun: Invite your whole team at no extra cost: everyone sees the agents at work and can answer them.

business.them: Moves data between apps; what to do with it is the Zap you draw.
business.rerun: Agents built for business jobs: {templates}+ for sales, inbox, invoices and reporting, that learn from every correction.

flexibility.them: 10,000+ apps, and each new case needs its own path.
flexibility.rerun: Handles new cases, runs scripts and a browser on its own machine, on any model.

pricing.them: Billed per task: 750 a month for $19.99, with AI, code and MCP calls on the same pool.
pricing.rerun: {price} a month, runs never counted: a secured machine, unlimited agents and model credit.

1.label: Setting it up
1.them: Pick a trigger, then add and map each step. Copilot can draft the Zap, and you maintain every step after that.
1.rerun: Describe the job in a sentence, like “triage my inbox every morning”. The agent plans the steps itself.

2.label: A case it has not seen
2.them: The Zap runs the same steps every time, so a new kind of email or record means another path or filter. A Zapier Agent decides for itself, within the 40 activities a run is allowed.
2.rerun: The agent reads each case, decides what it needs and asks you when it is unsure.

3.label: Files, code, a browser
3.them: Code runs as a step inside the Zap: 30 seconds included per step on Pro, then a task per extra 30-second block. No machine keeps files or a browser between runs.
3.rerun: Your workspace’s private machine: agents write files, run scripts, drive a browser and keep databases there between runs.

4.label: What it remembers
4.them: Each run starts blank. Anything to carry over goes into a Table or a storage step you build.
4.rerun: It writes down what you corrected and keeps its files and tables, so run 50 knows what run 1 learned.

5.label: The AI behind it
5.them: AI steps are billed in tasks by model tier, and Zapier’s own example puts one MCP tool call at 2 tasks.
5.rerun: Run on the Rerun model included in the plan, sign in with the ChatGPT or Claude plan you already pay for, or bring an API key.

6.label: While you are away
6.them: A Human in the Loop step pauses the Zap until a reviewer answers or the timeout runs out.
6.rerun: With Autopilot on, Rerun answers your agents within your rules, never for spending or deleting, and has a recap ready when you return.

7.label: What running it costs
7.them: Every action step is a task: 750 a month for $19.99 billed yearly. Zapier Agents are billed apart, in activities, 1,500 a month on Pro, and one run stops at 40 and asks you.
7.rerun: {price} a month for unlimited agents. Rerun counts neither runs nor steps.
